title: jmap: wire IPFS fetch into blob download endpoint (GET /jmap/download)
description:
Why: The blob download handler at GET /jmap/download/{accountId}/{blobId}/{name} already parses blobId as a CID and validates its format, but returns 501 Not Implemented. Wiring in the actual IPFS block fetch completes the endpoint and enables arbitrary CID retrieval — any CID reachable by the local IPFS node can be fetched by any authenticated client.

What:
1. Pass IpfsBlockStore into the blob_download handler via AppState.
2. Fetch the raw block bytes: ipfs.get_raw_block(&cid).await.
3. Wrap the bytes in a synthetic RFC 5322 MIME message and return that as the response body:
   - From: ipfs-gateway@<configured hostname>
   - Subject: IPFS:<cid>
   - Message-ID: <<cid>@ipfs.local>
   - X-Usenet-IPFS-CID: <cid>
   - MIME-Version: 1.0
   - Content-Type: application/octet-stream
   - Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64
   - Body: base64-encoded block bytes
4. HTTP Content-Type of the response: message/rfc822.
5. Return 404 if the CID is not found.
6. Authentication: respect whatever auth middleware is in place (tracked in stoa-37ad23c8.18).

Returning a synthetic RFC 5322 message rather than raw bytes keeps the format consistent with the NNTP XGET and IMAP X-USENET-IPFS-GET responses, and makes the content usable by standard HTTP clients that expect a message structure.
